note: Current access views and retained detector evidence figures. Source data and archived outputs are preserved; docs/data-and-figures.md inventories the active and retained visuals.

figures.evidence_type: deterministic toy assumptions; no observed travel times
figures.command: python analysis/plot_access_bounds.py && cd analysis/matlab && matlab -batch make_figures
figures.boundary: Deterministic shortest-time bounds and metadata qualification. No confidence intervals, real-area replication or observed accuracy. Reserved outcomes remain unopened.
figures.reproducibility: Read committed records only. plot_access_bounds.py writes the CSV exports, caption, Markdown tables and provenance; MATLAB R2025b draws the figure from bounds.csv and writes the table fragments, which are typeset with XeLaTeX or Tectonic (analysis/matlab/README.md). analysis/tests/test_access_figure.py checks the CSV exports, table fragments and caption against the record. Source and generator hashes are recorded in the derived provenance file; original evidence and its hashed generator unchanged.

figures.command: python analysis/plot_stress_cases.py && python analysis/demo_synthetic.py && cd analysis/matlab && matlab -batch make_figures
figures.boundary: Synthetic scene from make_scene(size=256, seed=1); demonstrates the extractor's behaviour, not performance on real imagery. Since CR-09 (2026-09-16) the blue lines are each candidate's delivered path_px (one interior-biased route per accepted component; no branch or junction recovery), not the legacy straight chord.
figures.reproducibility: Deterministic given the seed. Numeric output (scene fingerprint and candidate geometry) is pinned in results/method_demo_synthetic.numeric.json and gated by analysis/tests/test_demo_reproducibility.py. Do NOT gate on PNG bytes: font rasterisation differs between freetype builds, so the text bands change while every data pixel is identical -- see results/method_demo_synthetic.env.json. The rendered path geometry (path_px, path_length_px, candidate ids and order) is pinned in results/extractor_stress_cases.json under cases.demo_reference.exported_paths_px and checked by the same test module; method_demo_synthetic.numeric.json is retained as the legacy chord/scene record. results/method_demo_synthetic.env.json describes the pixel comparison of an earlier matplotlib render; the numeric gate it motivates is unchanged. The MATLAB figure draws results/figures/data/demo_reference.json; demo_synthetic.py checks that file against make_scene(size=256, seed=1).

figures.command: python analysis/plot_stress_cases.py && cd analysis/matlab && matlab -batch make_figures
figures.boundary: Five views of the CR-09 stress cases: the delivered path_px against the legacy endpoints_px chord and each case's reference centerline. Synthetic constructions with known truth; nothing here is imagery or a site result. Caption numbers are read from the v4 stress record, not typed.
figures.reproducibility: Deterministic given the fixed seeds in stress_cases.py. plot_stress_cases.py writes one JSON file per case (displayed field rounded to 0.01 z units, reference pixels, paths and chords) and the captions; MATLAB draws the PNG and PDF. analysis/tests/test_plot_stress_cases.py checks that the committed data files and captions match a fresh export and that the demo paths equal the record; pixels are not compared (font rasterisation differs between machines).

figure_comparison_policy.reason: For method-demo-synthetic, a committed-vs-fresh PNG diff shows 1.59% of pixels differing, all of it glyph rasterisation in the title and footer bands; every pixel inside both axes is identical. Comparing bytes would report drift that does not exist, and a real change in the scene or the extracted geometry would be lost in that noise.
figure_comparison_policy.verified_stable_across: numpy 2.1.3 / scipy 1.14.1 and numpy 2.4.6 / scipy 1.17.1 -- same scene sha256, same six candidate endpoints, byte-identical PNG
